- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.7) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; apply downward bias correction by 1–2% for next 5–7 days.
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., >+5% from prior 5-day avg), model often overshoots; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next 3–5 days to avoid overreaction.
- If sentiment turns negative (≤-0.3) mid-period, model frequently underestimates; increase forecast by 1–2% for next 3–7 days to counteract pessimism.
- Model exhibits strong mean reversion bias: if price deviates >±3% from 10-day moving average, adjust forecast toward that average within 3–5 days.
- For 30-day horizon, model consistently underestimates true outcomes when sentiment is mixed or negative; add 0.5–1.5% to forecast if sentiment average <0.5 over last 7 days.
- If official event (e.g., policy change, auction) occurs within 3 days, model often misses immediate reaction; adjust forecast upward or downward by 1–3% based on event direction and sentiment polarity.
